name: Creidne

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Creidne numbers among the gods of Ireland. He belonged to the artisan deities of the Tuatha Dé Danann, that magical race. His craft name was the brazier, and his trade lay in precious metals such as bronze and gold. With Goibniu and Luchtar he formed the na trí dée Dána, the three craft gods. Creidne forged the weapons his people carried against the Fomorians. Some tales call him the smith who shaped the silver hand of king Nuada after that ruler was hurt, while others give the credit to Dian Cécht. One legend says Creidne drowned while trying to bring gold in from Spain. A second figure of the same name was one of the Warrior Women who fought beside the Fianna.

okr.objective: Creidne is an Irish artisan god of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
key_results: He worked in bronze and gold as one of the three craft gods.
He forged weapons against the Fomorians.
Tales differ on whether he or Dian Cécht made Nuada's silver hand.
Reports of his drowning come from a gold import from Spain.
